Need for policy to combat Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR).
details:
Dr. Anil SukhdeoraoBonde:
 I seek to bring to the attention of the
Government, the growing threat of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), a silent
pandemic that is weakening our ability to treat common infections and
threatening the very foundation of modern medicine. India is among the world?s
highest consumers of antibiotics. Misuse and overuse in both humans and
animals, over-the-counter access, and poor waste management have made many
infections harder and more expensive to treat. In 2021, India recorded an
estimated 267,000 deaths directly attributable to AMR, with nearly a million
associated deaths, ranking 57th globally in AMR mortality This growing
resistance means longer hospital stays, higher treatment costs, and increased
mortality, particularly among older adults. It also poses a serious risk to
surgeries, cancer therapies, and intensive care, where effective antibiotics
are essential. While India has launched the National Action Plan on AMR 2.0,
challenges remain: poor surveillance, weak cross-sector coordination, unchecked
antibiotic use in agriculture and animal husbandry, and inadequate public
awareness
I urge the Government to ensure implementation of NAP-AMR 2.0 with dedicated
funding, strict regulation of antibiotic sales, and public education campaigns.
We must treat antibiotics as a shared national resource not as routine consumer
goods. Timely action on AMR is not just a health necessity it is a
national development imperative.
(ENDS)

records.title: Need to recognize Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) under the National Policy for Rare Diseases.
details:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde:
??????????? I draw attention of the
Government to the need for formal recognition and systematic care for patients
with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1), a rare and complex genetic condition
affecting approximately 1 in 3,000 to 5,000 people. NF1 often begins in childhood
and causes tumours, bone abnormalities, learning disabilities and, in many
cases, plexiform neurofibromas (PN) progressive nerve sheath tumours that can
lead to pain, disfigurement and life-threatening complications. The
psychosocial impact is profound, with patients facing stigma, bullying,
isolation and deep emotional distress.? Despite this, NF1 remains
under-recognised in India?s health policy, including the National Policy for
Rare Diseases (NPRD). This lack of recognition restricts access to multidisciplinary
care, innovative therapies, financial assistance, and structured
rehabilitation.? Current disability assessment frameworks also fail to capture
the invisible and fluctuating impairments caused by NF1.
??????????? Scientific progress now offers
effective, targeted therapies for inoperable PN. Yet, without NPRD inclusion,
such treatments remain inaccessible for most Indian patients.
??????????? I urge the Government to
formally include NF1 under the NPRD to enable standardized care at Centres of
Excellence, treatment funding, structured referrals, patient registries and
advocacy support. This is a public health and moral imperative. 
(ENDS)

records.title: Need for a Dedicated National Response for Type 1 Diabetes in India.
details:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde: There is an urgent
need for a dedicated national framework to support children and young adults
living with Type 1 Diabetes, a lifelong autoimmune condition that strikes early
and demands daily insulin and vigilant care. Unlike Type 2 diabetes, Type 1 is
not lifestyle-related and cannot be prevented.? It requires round-the-clock
access to insulin, glucometers, ketone strips, trained providers, and school
safety protocols. India has over 1 million people living with Type 1 Diabetes,
yet their needs are not fully integrated into public health programmes. ?Since they
do not fall under the ?rare? disease category and are relatively small in
number, they are often overlooked in NCD (Non-Communicable Diseases)
programmes. Meeting their needs is neither complex nor unaffordable. India
already manufactures world-class insulin used globally, I, therefore, urge the
Government to: 1.???? Create a national Type 1 Diabetes pathway with dedicated
budgets. 2.??????????? Ensure uninterrupted access to insulin and monitoring
tools across public facilities.3.??????? Mandate school safety protocols for
hypoglycaemia management.4. Strengthen device regulation and data systems for
better care outcomes. Type 1 Diabetes care is an opportunity to save lives,
uphold health equity, and make India a global leader in compassionate,
high-quality diabetes care.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand to adopt research-linked incentives for Med-Tech innovation.
details:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde:
??????????? There is urgent need to
support medical technology innovation through structured policy frameworks such
as Research-Linked Incentives (RLIs). As a medical professional. I believe
India stands at a defining moment in healthcare transformation. Demographic
shifts, digital acceleration, and increasing demand for affordable and
high-quality medical technologies require decisive policy interventions.
??????????? While the Production-Linked
Incentive (PLI) scheme has supported manufacturing, India still imports over
70% of high-end medical technologies. Significant gaps persist in design-led
R&D, clinical validation, IP monetization, and global competitiveness. The
National Policy on R&D and Innovation in Pharma-MedTech (2023) is a
positive step, but targeted support is needed to realize its vision truly. RLIs
provide structured incentives throughout the innovation lifecycle - from
prototyping to regulatory approval. A three-tiered framework aligned with
Technology Readiness Levels can provide milestone-based grants, co-funded
clinical trials in India, and tax benefits on patent royalties. This
complements national initiatives, such as the PRIP (Promotion of Research and
Innovation in Pharma MedTech Sector) scheme and the Anusandhan National
Research Foundation. 
Successful
R&D-linked incentive models already exist in sectors like semiconductors,
EVs, and pharmaceuticals. Globally, countries like the US and Singapore have
demonstrated the success of similar frameworks. With Indias MedTech sector
projected to grow from $12 billion in 2023 to $50 billion by 2030, we must act
now.
??????????? I urge the Government to adopt
RLIs and ensure long-term support for MedTech innovation, making "Innovate
in India" a practical reality.
(ENDS)

Demand for relief for exporters of Orange fruits from Vidarbha region in Maharashtra to Bangladesh.
details:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde: Sir,
you are aware that in Maharashtra State, Amravati and Nagpur Division is
recognized as Vidarbha. It is also the highest orange-fruit producer and
exporter in the country. Total 1,26,000 Hectares of area is occupied for
production of Oranges in Amravati and Nagpur Division.
Around seven lakh Metric Tonnes of Oranges are produced in the season of Ambiya
and Mriga bahar.The farmers and producer company exporters of this Division
have yearly been exporting around 1.25 to 1.50 lakh Metric Tonnes of Oranges to
Bangladesh. But, due to hike in Import Duty by Bangladesh Government from Rs.
32 to Rs. 62 per Kg, the Orange export to Bangladesh has totally been stopped
this season. Due to multiple-time hikes in Import Duty and devaluation of
currency of Bangladesh, total Orange export from Vidarbha has suffered.I urge
upon the Government to look into the matter and impress upon the Government of Bangladesh to reduce the
Import Duty or support Orange exporters by providing 25 to 30 per cent subsidy
to continue Orange export to Bangladesh.
(Ends)

records.title: Establishing Clinics for Sexual Problems at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in India.
details:
Dr.
Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde: Sexual health is a
fundamental aspect of overall well-being, yet sexual problems in males,
including impotency and various sexual disorders, remain significantly
prevalent in India. According to studies, approximately 52% of men between 40
to 70 years old experience some form of erectile dysfunction, with the
prevalence expected to rise due to lifestyle changes and increasing stress
levels. Moreover, the incidence of other sexual disorders like premature
ejaculation and low libido is also substantial, affecting the quality of life
and mental health of a significant portion of the male population.
Unfortunately, a substantial number of affected individuals seek treatment from
unqualified practitioners, leading to inadequate and non-evidence-based
management. Recognizing the urgency of addressing this issue, we propose the
establishment of specialized clinics for sexual problems at all All India
Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) locations across the country. These
clinics will adopt a multidisciplinary approach involving urologists,
endocrinologists, psychiatrists, and counsellors to provide comprehensive care
to patients.
